status.label: Reproduce launch-context difference
status.detail: WinGet-linked executables fail only in Terminal launched by PowerToys; direct launch and a resolved executable target work. No active owner or linked fix is present.

next_action.label: Compare Terminal activation contexts
next_action.reason: The public report already provides a discriminating symlink/direct-target and launch-route comparison.

reproduce.title: Compare WinGet executable links under PowerToys and direct Terminal activation
reproduce.module: PowerToys Run / Keyboard Manager app launch
reproduce.version_requirement: Latest stable first; historical PowerToys 0.79.0/0.82.1, WinGet 1.7.10582, Terminal 1.19 and PowerShell 7.4 references
prerequisites: Disposable Windows test account with Windows Terminal, PowerShell and a benign WinGet-installed package that exposes an executable link, such as fnm.
Close every Terminal process between routes so existing-window/process reuse does not hide the activation context.
Keep user identity and elevation constant and do not disable reparse-point trust protections.
steps: Install a test package through WinGet; record the generated link target and verify invoking the link works in a Terminal opened directly from Start.
Close Terminal fully; open it through PowerToys Run and invoke the same link with the same arguments, recording whether 'untrusted mount point' appears.
In that same PowerToys-launched shell, invoke the resolved target directly; compare success without modifying or replacing the link.

Repeat with a Keyboard Manager shortcut launching wt.exe as reported by the commenter; compare launch route, token/elevation, inherited environment and relevant process mitigation state using maintainer tools.
Repeat on the current stable build before applying any historical launch-path correction.
reproduce.expected_result: The same supported WinGet executable link works across activation routes. The trace must distinguish inherited launch context from PATH or executable-association errors before a patch is selected.

actions.label: Approve launch-context investigation
actions.note: Conditional plan; preserve Windows trust and elevation checks. No weakening of reparse-point security is proposed.

judgment.rationale: The report already supplies package/link, Terminal activation route, error text and direct-launch control. Maintainer-side process-context comparison is more useful than another log request.
evidence: The original report contrasts PowerToys Run activation with direct Terminal and Win+X activation.
The follow-up reproduces on 0.82.1, including Keyboard Manager launching wt.exe, and says the resolved target works: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/31739#issuecomment-2238146740
Live issue is open and unassigned; no timeline-linked fix or direct issue-number PR was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Run the controlled activation/link matrix and identify the inherited context difference before implementing the candidate.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys app-activation compatibility change may be applicable; no existing concrete fix attempt was identified in the reviewed public evidence.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve supported shell launch semantics for WinGet executable links
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: PowerToys-launched Terminal inherits a launch context or process policy that rejects traversal of the WinGet executable link, while direct shell activation does not. The specific token/mitigation difference is unconfirmed; direct-target success argues against a missing binary.
plan: Reproduce with all Terminal processes closed between runs and compare direct, Run and Keyboard Manager activation while holding user/elevation constant.
Trace the matching program result activation and shared process-start helpers; inspect the actual token/mitigation/environment difference rather than assuming UseShellExecute alone causes it.

If the difference originates in PowerToys, use the supported Windows activation path that preserves intended user/elevation semantics and normal link traversal; do not disable trust checks or resolve every user command link as a workaround.
Add regression coverage for executable link versus target, direct versus packaged Terminal activation, spaces in paths and existing Terminal process reuse.
verification: The same fnm link executes from all three activation routes without an untrusted-mount-point error.
Negative permission/trust cases still fail correctly, and no route unexpectedly elevates or changes user identity.

confidence.rationale: The route/link distinction is strong evidence, but no current process-context trace identifies the responsible PowerToys or OS boundary.

issue_context.summary: WinGet-created executable links fail inside Terminal launched through PowerToys Run or Keyboard Manager, while direct Terminal launch and executing the resolved target work.
known_information: Reported errors include 'untrusted mount point' and 'No application is associated'; the report gives exact package and tool versions.
The follow-up spans Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.4.2 on PowerToys 0.82.1.
Live labels identify PowerToys Run and app compatibility; there is no assignee.
inferences: A shared launch-context difference is more plausible than a Run search-index defect because Keyboard Manager also reproduces it.
The precise inherited token, policy or OS activation mechanism is not established.
issue_context.analysis: The report is already sufficiently discriminating for a local investigation. Ask maintainers to compare real process context, not reporters to perform security debugging or resend generic diagnostics.
initial_investigation: Read the complete report and full follow-up, including the direct-target workaround.
Enumerated the public timeline and direct issue-number PR search; no linked fix was identified.
Located program activation and process-start helper ownership under src/modules/launcher; these are investigation entry points, not proof of the failing branch.
No executable-link or process-context experiment was run during this pass.
